science.scope: Constructed continuous population scenarios, not observations of named species. A cycle is not a universal diagnostic of any interaction.
science.predation: Lotka-Volterra: dA=s(0.65A-0.009AB), dB=s(0.0032AB-0.38B), s=1.0936666666666668. One time-unit calibration produces about 3 complete orbits in t=0..36.
science.competition: dA=0.65A[1-(A+alpha B)/KA(t)], dB=0.65B[1-(B+beta A)/KB(t)]. KA=240[1+0.52 sin(2pi t/12)], KB=240[1-0.52 sin(2pi t/12)]. Default alpha=beta=0.6, settled periodic coexistence; exclusion alpha=0.25,beta=2.4 starts with both populations present. Both cross effects remain negative.
science.mutualism: Saturating mutualistic benefits plus self-limitation. Self-limitation is divided by E(t)=1+0.42 sin(2pi t/36). Obligate independent rates are -0.18,-0.15; facultative rates are +0.18,+0.15. Optional removal at t=18 sets only mutualistic benefit terms to zero; populations are not reset. The same environment continues after removal.
science.parasitism: H=hosts, P=total resident adult parasites, L=free-living infective stages. dH=0.5H-0.0015H^2-0.06P; dP=0.015HL-P[0.3+0.0015H+0.06+0.12P/H]; dL=2P-(0.015H+1.1)L. Negative-binomial aggregation k=1; density regulation enters host mortality. Right axis counts P, not infected hosts or L.
science.counterfactual: Parasite-free host reference uses the same H0=40 and host vital rates with P=L=0.
science.numerics: Deterministic RK4, step 0.03; intervention boundary split with left-limit endpoint evaluation. No artificial curve clamping, stitching or periodic population resets.
science.axes: Fixed linear domains include all relevant scenario and counterfactual values. Competition axes share a range; other dual axes need separate readings.
